limits: Unsupervised results are hard to validate: no accepted cross-validation or independent-test mechanism (p.504).
Number of PCs is chosen by eyeballing a scree plot; no objective rule for exploratory use (p.514).
Matrix completion assumes data missing at random; informative missingness invalidates it; Algorithm 12.1 is not guaranteed global optimum (p.515-516).
K-means finds local optimum only; hierarchical clustering assumes nested clusters (p.528).
Clustering forces every point into a cluster, so outliers distort; mixture models suggested instead (p.534).
Cluster p-value methods have no consensus, deferred to ESL (p.533).
Matrix completion on USArrests uses only 4 variables, the low end for the method (p.518).
practices: Center variables to mean zero before PCA (12.2.1).
Scale variables to sd 1 before PCA when units differ; may skip if all in same units such as gene expression (p.513).
Pick number of PCs by scree-plot elbow for exploration; treat as a tuning parameter via cross-validation in a supervised pipeline (p.514-515).
PC signs are arbitrary; compare software by direction only (p.514).
Use PC scores in place of raw features in regression/classification/clustering to reduce noise (p.515).
Impute missing values by Algorithm 12.1 only when missingness is random; choose M by holding out extra entries (p.515-518).
Run K-means many times from random starts (n_init 20 or 50) and keep the lowest objective; set random_state (p.524, 543).
Prefer average or complete linkage over single; avoid centroid linkage because of inversions (p.529).
Do not read similarity from horizontal proximity in a dendrogram; use fusion height (p.527).
Choose dissimilarity to fit the question: correlation distance for shopper preference profiles (p.530-531).
Try several standardization, linkage and K choices and cluster subsets to test robustness; report clusters as hypotheses, not truth (p.533-535).
